reviews.one_line_contribution: An 'admit everything once' shadow-store audit that, for the first time, measures the counterfactual value of memory items a write-gate would have bypassed and of items a pruning rule would have deleted, and reports admission-score rank correlation, false-bypass cost, harmful-item capture versus random pruning, and the number of feedback events a pruning decision needs to beat random.
reviews.closest_prior_work: Two threats, both verified via channel (a). (1) arXiv:2302.06960 'Data pruning and neural scaling laws: fundamental limitations of score-based algorithms' (TMLR, verified via s2cli paper) already proves, theoretically and empirically, that score-based selection degenerates to (or below) random in the regime where per-item scores are noisy, and that randomization/calibration is the fix; together with arXiv:2202.02643 'The Unreasonable Effectiveness of Random Pruning' (verified, also on the novelty card) this is the general form of P2 and P4 — 'a utility score prunes no better than random until its estimate is good enough.' It does not do it for agent memory, does not use an intervention ground truth on the same (game, seed), and has nothing to say about admission of items that are never stored, so it narrows the contribution to a transplant rather than killing it. (2) arXiv:2608.00017 'Memory Reward Inflation in Self-Improving LLM Agents' (verified via s2cli paper: self-graded reward inflation compounds even under plain similarity retrieval; LUCID de-inflation on BIRD) is the closest agent-side work and is the direct competitor for P5's entrenchment claim; the proposal's distinction (environment-verified rather than self-graded rewards) is real but makes P5 the least surprising half of the submission. Neither audits admission or pruning against realized per-item counterfactual value, so I found no work that makes the central claim.
reviews.strongest_objection: The headline is a null whose falsifier sits at or beyond the reliability ceiling of the ground truth it is measured against. Per-item SE is stated as ~0.10 (10 net) at 48 pairs; if the true between-item SD of realized ADD among success-filtered, same-type self-pool items is ~5 net — which Measurement C makes likely, since static3 already captures +12.4 net and the whole k=3 residual over it is only +17.2, leaving little item-specific variance — then reliability is ~0.2 and the maximum attainable raw Spearman is ~0.45. P1's falsifier ('any scorer reaches Spearman >= 0.4 with a bootstrap CI excluding 0.2') is then unreachable by construction, and the disattenuated 0.3 threshold divides by a reliability estimate that is itself noisy. The audit can return 'no scorer predicts realized value' without any scorer being wrong. E0 does not rescue this: it establishes value variance on a manufactured expert-versus-planted-W contrast (40 items each, ~2% of the candidate pool), not on the 160-candidate population where the null is claimed. This is precisely the failure that sank memory_item_value_reliability (6.12) in round 1 ('effect sizes below the noise floor'), and the proposal has not shown it escapes it. Compounding this, three of the remaining four predictions are weak by the proposal's own numbers: P2 is unresolvable (24-item strata give a capture-difference SE ~0.14 against a 0.15 threshold, measured against a reference set that is only the handful of E1 items with LOO <= -10); P3 is close to arithmetic (3,553 games x k=3 over ~1,932 items is a mean of ~5.5 events, so >=35% reaching >=8 is near-impossible under concentrated similarity x utility retrieval — the claim mostly restates the chosen pool-size-to-stream-length ratio); and P4's SF-AMS arm never sees outcomes, while the planted W items are same-type near-duplicates of expert items and therefore score high on SF-AMS's own redundancy term, so the test is decided by how the W class was built. Secondary: the episode arithmetic is understated ~2x. By the proposal's own cost model (40 items x 48 pairs x 2 arms = 3,840 episodes = 3.2 h), E1's 160 candidates cost 12.8 h, not 6.4; E0's 80 items cost 6.4 h, not 3.5; E3's 9 cells x 24 items x 32 pairs x 2 arms = 13,824 episodes cost ~11.5 h, not 5.8. The real total is ~45-50 h, not 25.
reviews.what_would_fix_it: Make reliability the first-class measurement rather than a correction factor. Run a gating cell before E1 that estimates the split-half reliability of realized ADD on the actual candidate population (self-pool successes), with a pre-registered minimum (e.g. reliability >= 0.4); below it, the finding is reported as 'item value is not measurable at this budget in this environment,' which is a legitimate and publishable result, not as 'admission scores fail.' Report every rank correlation as a fraction of the measured attainable ceiling, and state P1's falsifier in ceiling-relative terms. Add the supervised ceiling baseline below. Then: enlarge E3 strata to >=60 items with a stated MDE for a 0.15 capture difference, or collapse to two strata; replace P3 with a coverage curve over at least two store sizes (e.g. 500 vs 1,900 items) so the claim is not fixed by the chosen ratio; add a non-redundant planted-harm variant (a wrong procedure that duplicates no existing same-type item) and report the measured harm-redundancy correlation, so P4 is not decided by W-item construction; and correct the episode budget, which by the proposal's own per-class cost is roughly double what is stated.
reviews.missing_baseline: A cross-fitted supervised ceiling: fit a predictor of realized ADD on cheap write-time features using half of the E1 sample's measured values and evaluate it on the held-out half. Without it, P1's null cannot distinguish 'these three reconstructed scorers are bad' from 'realized item value is unpredictable from any write-time feature here' from 'realized value was never measured reliably enough to be predicted' — three findings with completely different implications for the memory literature, and only the first is the one the title claims. Also absent: a frequency-only pruning arm (bottom 20% by retrieval count), which is needed to separate usage from redundancy and recency inside SF-AMS and to connect to the archived utility_pruning_is_frequency_pruning result the proposal says it supersedes.
reviews.preprint_collision: No verified collision. Channel (a), s2cli.py (S2 + HF), answered every query; WebSearch was unavailable in this session and was not used. Queries I ran: (i) [--recent] 'memory admission score predicts realized counterfactual utility of stored item agent' -> A-MAC 2603.04549, Memory Reward Inflation 2608.00017, Compliance Trap 2607.10608, HiMPO 2606.16285, MEMPROBE 2606.24595; none measures score against counterfactual item value. (ii) 'randomized holdout audit of pruning rule versus random pruning leave-one-out realized value' -> the data/weight-pruning literature only: 2302.06960, 2210.15809, 2309.17310; nothing on agent memory. (iii) [--recent] 'false bypass rate memory write gating what happens to rejected memories agent shadow store' -> governance and poisoning work (GateMem 2606.18829, TRUSTMEM 2606.25161, 2605.26252); nothing on bypassed-item value. (iv) 'A-MAC adaptive memory admission control evaluation admitted versus rejected memory items downstream' -> A-MAC 2603.04549, MemoryRewardBench 2601.11969, Diagnosing Retrieval vs Utilization 2603.02473, MemFail 2605.26667; the closest named method's own evaluation does not follow rejected items. (v) 'score based selection beats random only above sample size threshold noisy value estimates winner curse data pruning' -> 2302.06960, 2606.27997; the home-literature form of P2/P4. (vi) [--recent] 'self-evolving agent memory utility reinforcement entrenches incorrect experiences retrieval frequency feedback loop' -> RoMeRL 2608.02508, MemRL 2601.03192, OPD-Evolver 2606.17628, MemEvolve 2512.18746; the loop is asserted in these papers, not measured against counterfactual value. ID verification: I verified 2603.04549 (A-MAC), 2603.14597, 2607.22562 (SF-AMS), 2604.00131 (Oblivion), 2512.10696 (ReMe), 2608.00017 (Memory Reward Inflation), 2302.06960 and 2202.02643 via s2cli paper/search. I could NOT verify arXiv:2509.12765 (the 'DIG confidence gain' scorer) — s2cli returns 'not found on S2 or HF,' and a targeted search for confidence-gain document scoring returned different papers instead (Information Gain Pruning 2601.17532, SePer 2503.01478, 2604.08920). That matters because DIG is one of the three write-time scorers whose failure is the headline, and the entailment check names it as the scorer most likely to reach the falsifying correlation. Two accuracy problems in the check itself: 2603.14597 is D-MEM, 'Dopamine-Gated Agentic Memory via Reward Prediction Error Routing' — a Fast/Slow routing architecture, not the 'RPE-critic router' with a critic-predicted-utility gate the proposal describes and reimplements as a logistic model on surprise and novelty; and the proposal concedes A-MAC's weights and the critic are reconstructed from abstracts, so the headline null is about the authors' reimplementations, and a reviewer will read it as a straw man unless released code is run. Judging the check overall: it is unusually thorough for this pool — six classed queries, IDs, a home-vocabulary query, and one paper (2608.00017) actually verified rather than cited — and it is right that no agent-memory work audits admission or pruning against realized value. Its gap is the home literature it did search but did not connect: 2302.06960 and 2202.02643 already establish 'score-based selection is no better than random when the score is noisy,' which is the general claim P2 and P4 test, and the check does not name them or say what its agent-side instance adds beyond the setting.
